CASE FILE — Jack Daniel's Properties, Inc. v. VIP Products LLC
Docket: 22-148 | Term: OT2022 | Court below: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
Parties: Jack Daniel's Properties, Inc.v. VIP Products LLC (Petitioner v. Respondent)
Question presented: Is humorous use of another’s trademark as one’s own on a commercial product subject to the Lanham Act’s likelihood-of-confusion analysis, or instead entitled to heightened First Amendment protection?
Facts: VIP Products LLC, a company that manufactures dog toys, created a plastic toy that resembles Jack Daniel’s iconic bottle. Instead of “Jack Daniel’s,” the toy’s “label” says “Bad Spaniels”; and instead of “Old No. 7” and “Tennessee Sour Mash Whiskey” it says “The Old No. 2 on your Tennessee Carpet.” Jack Daniel’s sued the toy company alleging violation of its trademark. The district court held that the toy is a humorous parody entitled to First Amendment protection, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit affirmed.
Posture: Writ of certiorari
